response.sql:
WITH per_gender AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT i.order_id) AS invoiced_orders
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN Orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN Invoices i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
), above_average AS (
    SELECT invoiced_orders
    FROM per_gender
    WHERE invoiced_orders > (SELECT AVG(invoiced_orders * 1.0) FROM per_gender)
)
SELECT AVG(invoiced_orders * 1.0) AS average_figure,
       AVG(invoiced_orders * 1.0) - (SELECT AVG(invoiced_orders * 1.0) FROM per_gender) AS average_excess
FROM above_average;

assumptions.assumption: Counts distinct orders that have at least one invoice, grouped by the gender of the customer who placed them; NULL gender is retained as a group. Customers with no invoiced orders are excluded because they contribute no rows through the required invoice-to-order joins.
